prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the near counter and people from the darker walls, ceiling, and display cases: the counter is generally within about 0.3–1 m, nearby people about 0.5–2 m, and background surfaces roughly 2–5 m away. Across the five frames, the closest person shifts from the left/front to the right/front and then fills much of the final view, while other people remain farther behind the counter; overlapping depth silhouettes show that the counter and nearest bodies occlude them. Bright foreground regions also reveal that the counter, basket, and nearby hands are within arm’s reach, whereas the people behind the counter are usually separated from the wearer by roughly the counter’s width. The map is unreliable at silhouettes, merges adjacent people and counter surfaces, and gives only approximate relative depth rather than trustworthy metric distances or facing direction.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies people in every frame and intermittently labels a TV/display, cup, book, and remote, making their left/right arrangement and overlap clearer than in RGB: people occupy the foreground and middle distance, while the small objects lie on or just above the counter. In the second frame, two people stand close together behind the counter, roughly 0.5–1 m apart and about 1–2 m from the wearer; later, a foreground person enters from the right, becomes partly out of view, and occludes much of the scene at an estimated distance below 1 m. The cup, book, and remote appear within arm’s reach of the wearer or the nearest person, with the book and remote below the TV and the people extending above them. Metric distance and facing are not encoded, and the map is unreliable because it misses major structures such as the counter, basket, display cases, and some people or body parts, while several masks have coarse or truncated boundaries.
descriptions.pose: The pose map exposes body and hand geometry that is difficult to isolate in RGB: one middle-distance person in the second frame has a visible upright torso and bent arms, and the later foreground figure has a larger, partly cropped skeleton consistent with being closer to the wearer. Head keypoints and torso orientation suggest that the clearest second-frame person faces generally toward the camera wearer, while several other people cannot be assigned a reliable facing direction because only scattered head or hand points are detected. Magenta hand clusters lie near the counter plane and within roughly 0.5–1 m of nearby bodies, indicating reach-scale separations; in later frames the closest hands and torso shift from centre-right toward the centre as the wearer or person turns. The map is highly incomplete: limbs disappear behind the counter or other bodies, cropped people extend out of frame, false or floating keypoints occur, and the sparse skeletons do not support dependable metric distances or gaze estimates.
